title: Day-of-week 0

normative.title: crontab(5), Vixie/cronie lineage
normative.quote: day of week (0 - 7) (0 or 7 is Sunday, or use names)

cases.label: monday-zero
cases.note: APScheduler 3.x from_crontab(): 0=MON..6=SUN and 7 is out of range. Named days (SUN, MON) stay Sunday-based in the same engine, so numeric and named spellings of one weekday disagree.

cases.label: posix-zero-only
cases.note: POSIX fixes day-of-week at [0,6] with 0=Sunday and admits no 7.

cases.label: quartz-1-7
cases.note: Quartz/AWS/Cloudflare: 1=SUN..7=SAT, so this literal names a different weekday.

expect.note: A numeral copied from a Vixie crontab into a Quartz scheduler fires on the wrong day every week, forever, with no error at any layer.

cron-parser[strict]@tzle2026a.error: Error: Invalid cron expression, expected 6 fields

rationale: Two incompatible numbering bases with overlapping legal ranges, so the same literal is valid in both dialects and silently means a different weekday. This is the highest-severity silent-mistranslation vector in the corpus.

title: Wrapping named day range FRI-MON

normative.title: POSIX.1-2017 crontab
normative.quote: Ranges of numbers are allowed. ... two numbers separated with a hyphen

cases.label: wrap-modulo
cases.note: Dialects that wrap a reversed range around the field bounds (croner, some Quartz ports, cron_descriptor).

apscheduler3@tz2026a.error: ValueError: The minimum value in a range must not be higher than the maximum

apscheduler3@tz2026c.error: ValueError: The minimum value in a range must not be higher than the maximum

cron-parser[strict]@tzle2026a.error: Error: Invalid cron expression, expected 6 fields

croner@tzle2026a.error: TypeError: CronPattern: From value is larger than to value: '5-1'

croner[legacyMode=false]@tzle2026a.error: TypeError: CronPattern: From value is larger than to value: '5-1'

robfig-cron@tz2026a.error: beginning of range (5) beyond end of range (1): FRI-MON

rationale: Neither POSIX nor crontab(5) says what a reversed range means. Vixie's parser rejects it; several dialects wrap modulo the field. 'Friday through Monday' is a phrase users write; the corpus must record that it is not portable.

title: Numeric and named spellings of the same weekday must agree (0 vs SUN)

normative.title: crontab(5), Vixie/cronie lineage
normative.quote: Names can also be used for the 'month' and 'day of week' fields.
normative.note: crontab(5) presents names as an alternative spelling of the numbers, not a second numbering

expect.note: Must equal the result of '0 12 * * SUN' in the same engine. An engine whose numeric and named day-of-week fields use different bases fails this vector while passing every named-day vector.

cron-parser[strict]@tzle2026a.error: Error: Invalid cron expression, expected 6 fields

rationale: Measured, not hypothetical: APScheduler 3.11.3's from_crontab() maps numeric 0 to Monday while mapping the name SUN to Sunday, so the two spellings of 'Sunday' in one engine denote different days. Because the corpus scores numeric and named vectors separately, this vector is what makes the inconsistency visible as a single failure.
